brief: CEG announced a 20-year PPA with GOOGL for 890 MWs of new nuclear uprates across PJM plants plus a 15-year offtake for 2,700 MWs of existing nuclear capacity, totaling 3.6 GWs within CEG's targeted $20-50/MWh premium to the PTC floor. This follows the AMZN deal at Calvert Cliffs (190 MWs new uprates, 500 MWs existing, after a co-located arrangement was rebuffed and the deal pivoted to front-of-the-meter) and Q2's 890/30 MWs, giving CEG nuclear contracts with all four hyperscalers and leaving its nuclear uprates fully contracted. Total contracted existing capacity reaches 4.1 GWs, which Wolfe estimates lifts EPS upside to base earnings by $1.70-2.40 at a $25-35/MWh premium to the PTC floor and $0.35-0.71 to overall earnings at a $5-10/MWh premium to market, shifting the base-EPS mix from 65-70% toward 75%+. The carbon-free fleet is now ~45% contracted. Ramp timing is long-dated (Calvert Cliffs 2030/2032, GOOGL mostly 2030+), so Wolfe frames this as longer-dated EPS upside plus a higher-multiple infrastructure rerate. ECP's post-close sale of 3M CEG shares is flagged as a minor sentiment headwind. Wolfe rates CEG Outperform, $395 price target (16x 2030E EPS of $19.39 plus 50% chance of $30/MWh additional margin).
